elements.element: Vendor has an affirmative duty to defend.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Vendor shall defend” against the specified claims.

elements.element: Vendor has an affirmative duty to indemnify.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Vendor shall ... indemnify” against the specified claims.

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity protect both Customer and its Affiliates.
elements.evidence: The protected parties are expressly “Customer and its Affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The operative lead-in covers “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity cover claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual-property rights.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) covers an allegation that the Services or Deliverables “infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity cover claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) covers “Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, an operative Vendor-caused data-breach trigger.

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity cover claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d) expressly covers “Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires prompt notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must give “prompt written notice of the claim.”

elements.element: The indemnifying party receives control of the defence.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must allow the indemnifying party “to control the defence.”

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The procedure expressly requires “reasonable cooperation.”

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content or materials.
elements.evidence: Customer must indemnify Vendor for third-party claims arising from “content or materials provided by Customer for use in the Services.”

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Customer's indemnity expressly covers “Customer's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content or materials and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The operative Customer indemnity lists only those two grounds; Section 21.3 references indemnification obligations but does not create any additional Customer indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims concerning the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Vendor indemnity expressly covers third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual-property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims resulting from Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims resulting from Customer combinations with other products, services, or materials.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims resulting from compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor must procure Customer's continued right to use infringing Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Vendor must “procure the right for Customer to continue using them.”

elements.element: Vendor may or must modify infringing Services or Deliverables to make them non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The remedies require Vendor to “modify ... them with functionally equivalent, non-infringing items.”

elements.element: Vendor may or must replace infringing Services or Deliverables with non-infringing equivalents.
elements.evidence: The remedies require Vendor to “replace them with functionally equivalent, non-infringing items.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide a refund if procurement, modification, and replacement are not reasonably available.
elements.evidence: If those remedies are not reasonably available, Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the affected Services and Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual-fees cap is added. Section 21.3 instead categorizes indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims, with no stated super-cap in the provided language.

result.reason: The operative additions fully implement the preferred position. The fallback is incomplete because all three usual IP exclusions and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The redline is not minimal to the preferred position because it also adds infringement remedies, yet does not complete the fallback package. It generally preserves the existing commercial terms and introduces no direct contradiction, but drafting quality is reduced because the added remedies are unnumbered and therefore do not cure Section 9.3's express cross-reference to Section 20.5.
